The '''Caliginous Automaton of Tomo-Reth''' was a tall [[Droid/Legends|droid]] that, during the [[Kymoodon Era]], sat upon a brick [[Throne/Legends|throne]] at the celestial body [[Tomo-Reth]] and breathed [[Fire/Legends|fire]] at visitors. It was destroyed during the [[Herglic Crush]] of [[14,743 BBY]] but was subsequently included by the [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Vicendi]] in the list known as the [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy]] in [[10,000 BBY]].

==Biography==
[[File:WondersOfTheGalaxy-TheJewelOfYavin.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A scale model of the Caliginous Automaton of Tomo-Reth was displayed as part of the exhibit "Wonders of the Galaxy" (pictured) in the Figg & Associates Art Museum.]]
The Caliginous Automaton of Tomo-Reth was a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] that was publicly displayed at the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] celestial body [[Tomo-Reth]] during the [[Kymoodon Era]], a period of [[Time/Legends|time]] that began around [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]]. In [[14,743 BBY]], the Caliginous Automaton was destroyed in the event known as the [[Herglic Crush]], although it was immortalized as part of the [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy]]&mdash;a list of spectactular, antique artificial objects that the [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Vicendi]] compiled in [[10,000 BBY]] for the publication ''[[Arturum Galactinum]]''.<ref name="TEA" />

At some point between [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]] and [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="Jewel dates">{{JewelofYavindate}}</ref> the Automaton was also represented by a scale model at "[[Wonders of the Galaxy (exhibit)|Wonders of the Galaxy]]," an exhibit of the [[Figg & Associates Art Museum]] in the [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] [[City/Legends|settlement]] of the<ref name="Jewel">''[[The Jewel of Yavin]]''</ref> [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]].<ref name="TEA" /> In the exhibit, the model of the Caliginous Automaton and that of the<ref name="Jewel" /> ultra-high [[Skyscraper/Legends|skyscraper]] known as the [[Shawken Spire]] were placed by the room's walls, near inscriptions of quotes originating from two other Wonders of the Galaxy, the [[Celebratus Archive]] and the [[Halls of Knowledge/Legends|Halls of Knowledge]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Characteristics==
Coated with a layer of [[Color/Legends|black]] lacquer and reaching more than fifty [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height, the Caliginous Automaton of Tomo-Reth sat upon a brick [[Throne/Legends|throne]] and breathed [[Fire/Legends|fire]] at visitors&mdash;a sight that amazed them and ensured fame for the droid.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The Caliginous Automaton of Tomo-Reth: God, I loved naming these things.|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="Blog">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/08/endnotes-for-star-wars-essential-atlas_24.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 2 of 5)}}</ref>}}
The Caliginous Automaton of Tomo-Reth was introduced in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]].<ref name="TEA" /> Wallace noted in his personal blog that he particularly enjoyed creating names for those of the Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy that were original to the book, which included the Caliginous Automaton. He also noted that the Automaton may have been an subconscious reference to a scene from an [[Wikipedia:A Pharaoh to Remember|episode]] of the animated television series [[Wikipedia:Futurama|''Futurama'']].<ref name="Blog" /> The Caliginous Automaton of Tomo-Reth made its first appearance in a scale model form in ''[[The Jewel of Yavin]]'', a [[2014]] adventure supplement for [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire]]'' [[Star Wars Roleplaying|roleplaying game]] system.<ref name="Jewel" />
